title: Hash collisions

problem.name: Hash collisions
problem.statement_latex: Given a random function $H$ with $n$-bit outputs and a sufficiently large domain, find distinct $x,x'$ with $H(x)=H(x')$. Collision resistance is the relevant property for many hash-based constructions and commitment schemes. The random-function comparison measures hash-oracle queries; total quantum time additionally counts coherent table access, and explicit circuits use gate or bit complexity.
problem.statement_text: Given a random function $H$ with $n$-bit outputs and a sufficiently large domain, find distinct $x,x'$ with $H(x)=H(x')$. Collision resistance is the relevant property for many hash-based constructions and commitment schemes. The random-function comparison measures hash-oracle queries; total quantum time additionally counts coherent table access, and explicit circuits use gate or bit complexity.

quantum.headline_latex: $O(r+\sqrt{2^n/r})$ queries with a table of $r$ values, Brassard--H\o yer--Tapp collision search.
quantum.headline_text: $O(r+\sqrt{2^n/r})$ queries with a table of $r$ values, Brassard–Høyer–Tapp collision search.
quantum.details_latex: The table parameter satisfies $1\le r\le 2^n$. Optimizing it gives $r=2^{n/3}$ and the tight $\Theta(2^{n/3})$ quantum query bound. Near-matching time assumes efficient coherent lookup into the stored table. A gate implementation includes the lookup circuit and reversible hash cost. The random-function setting yields the matching quantum collision lower-bound scale.

classical.headline_latex: $\Theta(2^{n/2})$ queries, birthday search or Pollard-rho collision finding.
classical.headline_text: $\Theta(2^{n/2})$ queries, birthday search or Pollard-rho collision finding.
classical.details_latex: Birthday storage is of order $2^{n/2}$ entries; Pollard-rho offers low-memory collision finding under the usual random-function assumptions. For a hash given by a $G$-gate circuit on $\ell$ input bits, the predicate $x\ne x'$, $H(x)=H(x')$ has $O(\ell+n+G)$ gates. Boolean tensor contraction and witness recovery give $\operatorname{poly}(\ell+n+G)2^{O((\ell+n+G)/\sqrt{\log(\ell+n+G)})}$ classical time. A linear-size explicit family therefore has a subexponential comparator.

strength.description_latex: Polynomial speedup of degree $3/2$ relative to the classical birthday query count. The BHT construction combines a stored table with Grover search. In output length $n$, the exponent changes from $1/2$ to $1/3$ without power saving.

evidence.description_latex: Fully proved in the collision-oracle model with the stated domain promise; random-function collision bounds give the corresponding cryptographic query scale.

hardware.description_latex:
The time-efficient BHT implementation stores about $2^{n/3}$ entries with coherent access and requires exponentially many fault-tolerant operations. Polynomial-qubit alternatives use different time-memory tradeoffs; the lookup model is a material resource assumption.

{\small [Before ``ETH is false'', the generic collision comparison used $\Theta(2^{n/2})$ classical versus $\Theta(2^{n/3})$ quantum queries, an exponential-constant improvement also used for explicit hash circuits.]\par}
